book.forgeweave.armor.casting.text:
Metal plating is cast at the Smeltery like any other metal part, which needs a plating cast, and a cast is made by pouring gold over a finished part.

Obsidian plating is the way in: the Part Builder carves obsidian into plating with a plating pattern. Set that plating on a Casting Table and pour gold over it for a plating cast, then cast iron and every other metal from there. The maille cast is made the same way from any Part Builder maille.
book.forgeweave.armor.casting.title: Casting Plating
book.forgeweave.armor.intro.text:
Armor is built the way tools are: from parts, at the Armor Station, out of the materials you choose. Every piece has a limited number of modifier slots and carries its materials' traits.

Unlike a tool, armor does nothing in the hand: its stats, traits and modifiers only work while it is worn.
book.forgeweave.armor.intro.title: Armor
book.forgeweave.armor.modifiers.text:
Armor takes modifiers at the Armor Station the way tools do at the Tool Station, from the same slot pool. Some fit armor alone: Fire, Blast, Projectile, Magic and Melee Protection each reduce one kind of damage, stacking across the worn set up to a cap; Knockback Resistance keeps you on your feet; Thorns hurts whatever hits you.

The general modifiers (Reinforced, Mending Moss, Soulbound and the extra modifier slot) fit armor as well. See the Modifiers chapter for each one.
book.forgeweave.armor.modifiers.title: Armor Modifiers
book.forgeweave.armor.parts.text:
Each piece is two parts. The plating is the outer shell and sets every stat: durability, armor, toughness and knockback resistance, with a separate plating shape for the helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots. Only sturdy materials make plating: the metals, obsidian and a few others.

The maille is the chain worn underneath. It has no stats of its own; it brings its material's traits and shows through the plating's gaps. Softer materials such as vine, bone and cactus can be woven into maille.
book.forgeweave.armor.parts.title: Plating and Maille
book.forgeweave.armor.traits.text:
Some materials carry a trait that only wakes on armor: iron's plating shrugs off projectiles, obsidian's explosions, cobalt's blows in melee, copper's the crushing dark below sea level. Manyullyn is warded against magic, amethyst bronze strikes back at the crystalline, silver is consecrated against the undead, knightslime shields with overslime.

Maille brings traits too: cactus is thorned, bone pierces guards, chorus sends attackers elsewhere, and blue slime vine slows your fall. Each material's page lists what it grants.
book.forgeweave.armor.traits.title: Armor Traits
book.forgeweave.intro.armor_station.text:
A blank pattern over a Tool Station makes the Armor Station, the Tool Station's sibling for plating and maille. It builds every armor piece, repairs and renames them, and applies their modifiers, the same way the Tool Station does for tools.

The Tool Station and Tool Forge no longer build armor at all; the two families finally each have their own workbench.
book.forgeweave.intro.blank_pattern.text:
Two planks and two sticks craft into four blank patterns. A blank pattern is a slate waiting for a shape: the Stencil Table stamps a part's outline into it, and one laid over a log or a crafting table builds the workshop's own stations.

A blank pattern and a book also bind this very guide.
book.forgeweave.intro.crafting_station.t:
A crafting table converts directly into a Crafting Station. It crafts exactly as the table it came from, except an unfinished project stays in the grid when you walk away.

A chest set beside the station shows its contents alongside the grid, so materials never need to leave storage to be used.
book.forgeweave.intro.part_builder.text:
Built from a blank pattern over a log. Lay a stamped pattern and a non-metal material on it and it carves the material into that part, showing the cost and the finished part's stats before you commit.

Metal is not carved; molten metal is cast into parts at the Smeltery.
book.forgeweave.intro.part_builder.title: Part Builder
book.forgeweave.intro.part_chest.text: Holds spare tool parts, and nothing else. Like the workshop's other chests it shows its contents in a neighbouring station's side panel, so a part carved yesterday is at hand when today's tool wants it.
book.forgeweave.intro.part_chest.title: Part Chest
book.forgeweave.intro.pattern_chest.text:
Stores one copy of each pattern, or of casts if you would rather; a chest holds one kind or the other, never both at once.

Set next to a Stencil Table or Part Builder, its contents appear right in that station's screen.
book.forgeweave.intro.stencil_table.text:
Built from a blank pattern over planks. Place a blank pattern in the table and pick a shape from the list to stamp it; every part the workshop knows has a stencil here.

A Pattern Chest beside the table shows on its right, so a fresh stencil can go straight into storage.
book.forgeweave.intro.tool_forge.text: The Tool Station's sturdier sibling: seared bricks and metal blocks built around a Tool Station. It does everything the station does, and it alone assembles the large tools: the hammer, the cleaver and their kin.
book.forgeweave.intro.tool_forge.title: Tool Forge
book.forgeweave.intro.tool_station.text:
A blank pattern over a crafting table makes the Tool Station, the heart of the workshop. Pick a tool from its sidebar, set the parts, and read the finished stats before you build.

The station also repairs, renames, and applies modifiers; the Modifiers chapter covers those.
book.forgeweave.intro.tool_station.title: Tool Station
book.forgeweave.intro.welcome.text:
Welcome to Materials and You: surviving the first day and beyond. Within these pages you will find the first steps to making tools from the materials you gather.

The first step is to craft a blank pattern. It is a blank slate to stamp a shape into, providing a reference for future creations.

This book grows with the workshop; check back occasionally for new chapters.
book.forgeweave.intro.welcome.title: Surviving the First Day
book.forgeweave.intro.workshop.text:
Shape a non-metal material in the Part Builder with a pattern, then combine the finished parts at the Tool Station. Patterns keep in the Pattern Chest and spare parts in the Part Chest. A crafting table converts into a Crafting Station that holds an unfinished project while you step away.

Together these make the Tool Workshop; they work best side by side. The Tool Forge, the station's sturdier sibling, is needed for the largest tools.
book.forgeweave.intro.workshop.title: The Tool Workshop
book.forgeweave.material.craft_partbuild: Can be crafted in the Part Builder
book.forgeweave.materials.intro.text:
Every part of a tool contributes the stats of the material it is made from: the head brings durability, mining speed and attack; the handle multiplies durability; a binding adds a flat bonus.

Materials also grant traits: special behaviours listed on the pages that follow.
book.forgeweave.materials.intro.title: Materials
book.forgeweave.modifiers.intro.text:
A finished tool is never truly finished. At the Tool Station or Tool Forge, sacrifice items to imbue a tool with modifiers. Each tool starts with a limited number of free slots, and some modifiers can be applied repeatedly for a stronger effect.

The pages that follow list every modifier known to this workshop.
book.forgeweave.modifiers.intro.title: Modifiers
book.forgeweave.smeltery.intro.text: There are many smelteries, but this one is yours, and it melts things really well.
book.forgeweave.smeltery.intro.title: The Smeltery
book.forgeweave.smeltery.structure.text:
The smeltery's interior can be any size up to 9x9, with walls as short as a single block or as tall as you like. A larger structure holds more molten metal at once. The structure needs a complete seared floor, but no ceiling.

The walls are built from seared bricks, seared glass, tanks and drains, with the core set into a wall; the floor must be solely seared blocks. At least one seared tank is required to hold fuel (lava works nicely), and faucets attach to drains to pour fluids out.
book.forgeweave.smeltery.structure.title: Building the Smeltery
book.forgeweave.smeltery.working.text:
Place ore or metal into the smeltery through its core and it slowly melts down. Different molten metals pool together below; some combinations mix into alloys.

Drain the result through a faucet into a Casting Table holding a cast to shape tool parts and ingots, or into a Casting Basin for full blocks.
book.forgeweave.smeltery.working.title: Working the Smeltery
book.forgeweave.subtitle: Surviving the first day and beyond
book.forgeweave.title: Materials and You
book.forgeweave.tools.repairing.text:
As you use your tools they take damage, and once all of their durability is gone they break. To fix that, repair your tool; there is no need to wait until it breaks.

Put the tool into a Tool Station or Tool Forge and add material matching the tool's head. If the head is made of several materials, any of them will do, and repairing with several at once grants bonus durability.
book.forgeweave.tools.repairing.title: Repairing

forgeweave.ponder.armor.text_1: Armor is assembled at the Armor Station, the Tool Station's sibling
forgeweave.ponder.armor.text_2: Each piece takes a plating shaped for it, which sets all of its stats
forgeweave.ponder.armor.text_3: And a maille, which adds its material's traits and shows through the plating
forgeweave.ponder.armor.text_4: The station builds the piece from the two parts

forgeweave.ponder.casting.text_1: A Seared Drain in a smeltery's wall is where the melt comes out
forgeweave.ponder.casting.text_2: Place a Faucet on the drain. Right-click it and it pours one ingot's worth of the selected melt out of its spout
forgeweave.ponder.casting.text_3: Seared Channels carry it sideways. Placing one against another chains them; right-click an arm to change its direction, or the top to open the bottom
forgeweave.ponder.casting.text_4: An open bottom pours into whatever waits below: a Casting Table holding a cast makes ingots and parts, a Casting Basin makes blocks
forgeweave.ponder.casting.text_5: The melt runs down the channels and fills the table and the basin. Keep pouring until they are full, then let them cool
forgeweave.ponder.casting.text_6: Once cooled, right-click to take the result out. The cast stays in the table for the next pour
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery.text_1: A smeltery is built from seared blocks. Start with a floor beneath the space that will hold the melt
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery.text_2: Raise walls at least two blocks tall around the interior. The corner columns are optional
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery.text_3: At least one Seared Tank must be part of the walls. It holds the fuel, such as lava, that heats the smeltery
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery.text_4: Complete the structure by placing a Standard Core in one of the walls, facing outward
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery.text_5: Once the structure is complete the core lights up: the smeltery is formed and ready to melt
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery_sizes.text_1: The smallest smeltery has a 1x1 interior: a 3x3 floor and walls two blocks tall, one of them a tank, one the core
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery_sizes.text_2: The interior can be any rectangle up to 9x9, and the walls as tall as you like. A bigger interior holds more melt
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery_sizes.text_3: Seared stairs and slabs are not smeltery walls or floor. The walls end below the first layer that holds one, and the interior shrinks with them
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery_sizes.text_4: Only the Seared Furnace's ceiling accepts them, laid bottom-half over the interior. Use full seared blocks here
forgeweave.ponder.smeltery_sizes.text_5: Either size forms the same way: the core lights up once the floor, walls and tank are all in place

gui.forgeweave.tool_station.repair.descr: Place a damaged tool in the middle slot and the material its head is made of alongside it to restore durability. A repaired tool keeps its parts, its stats and its traits. The same slots take modifier reagents: a tool has three modifier slots, and levelling a modifier up stays inside the slot it already occupies.

item.forgeweave.arrow.description: The Arrows are the ammo used for Forgeweave's Bows. One stack provides many shots, and they can be modified as any tool.
item.forgeweave.battleaxe.description: Two heavy heads on one haft. A fully charged swing carries through everything in a short arc in front of you, and staggers whatever it lands on.
item.forgeweave.battleaxe.property.1: Two heads, both counted in the damage
item.forgeweave.battleaxe.property.2: A fully charged swing hits everything in a short arc
item.forgeweave.battlesign.description: A broad slab on a stick. Hold right-click to block; an arrow caught head-on is sent back at whoever fired it.
item.forgeweave.boots.description: Plating over maille. The plating sets every stat; the maille brings its material's traits.
item.forgeweave.broadsword.description: A balanced sword. A solid, grounded blow carries to everything nearby, and right-click raises a brief parry that turns aside one blow and slows whoever threw it.
item.forgeweave.chestplate.description: Plating over maille. The plating sets every stat; the maille brings its material's traits.
item.forgeweave.cleaver.description: A massive blade for hewing through foes. Slow to swing, but a killing blow is far more likely to claim the victim's head.
item.forgeweave.crossbow.description: The Crossbow is a slow but very powerful weapon. It has to be loaded beforehand by holding right click, but can be fired at any moment afterwards. Fires vanilla arrows.
item.forgeweave.crossbow.property.1: Needs to be loaded before firing
item.forgeweave.dagger.description: A short, fast blade. Strike from behind and it bites far deeper than its size suggests.
item.forgeweave.dagger.property.1: Backstab: up to double damage from behind
item.forgeweave.excavator.description: Moves a 3x3 of earth at a time, and knocks anything in the way flat.
item.forgeweave.excavator.property.3: Effective on dirt, sand and gravel
item.forgeweave.frying_pan.description: Heavy, flat and loud. Its blows send whatever they land on flying.
item.forgeweave.hammer.description: Breaks a 3x3 of stone at once, slowly. Leaves what it hits reeling.
item.forgeweave.hatchet.description: Fells trees, and doubles as a weapon in a pinch.
item.forgeweave.heavy_boots.description: Plating over maille, backed by a large plate. Armor is 1.4x the plating's; every piece worn slows you by 5%.
item.forgeweave.heavy_chestplate.descrip: Plating over maille, backed by a large plate. Armor is 1.4x the plating's; every piece worn slows you by 5%.
item.forgeweave.heavy_helmet.description: Plating over maille, backed by a large plate. Armor is 1.4x the plating's; every piece worn slows you by 5%.
item.forgeweave.heavy_leggings.descripti: Plating over maille, backed by a large plate. Armor is 1.4x the plating's; every piece worn slows you by 5%.
item.forgeweave.helmet.description: Plating over maille. The plating sets every stat; the maille brings its material's traits.
item.forgeweave.kama.description: Shears sheep and harvests+replants mature crops at a right-click. Deals extra damage against targets already at low health.
item.forgeweave.katana.description: A long, single-edged blade. Every blow that lands makes the next one hit harder, until you stop swinging.
item.forgeweave.katana.property.0: Every landed hit makes the next hit harder
item.forgeweave.katana.property.2: Lapses after five seconds without a hit
item.forgeweave.leggings.description: Plating over maille. The plating sets every stat; the maille brings its material's traits.
item.forgeweave.longbow.description: The Longbow is a powerful long range weapon. It provides high damage but is less mobile than its short brother. Uses material and vanilla arrows.
item.forgeweave.longsword.description: A long blade with reach. Hold right-click to charge, then release to leap in the direction you are looking.
item.forgeweave.lumberaxe.description: Fells a whole tree in one swing, and hits hardest on the first blow.
item.forgeweave.lumberaxe.property.2: Fells whole trees in one swoop
item.forgeweave.mattock.description: An axe and a shovel in one head. Tills soil like a hoe, and its heft carries a chance of a strong knockback on hit.
item.forgeweave.pickaxe.description: A basic mining tool. Digs stone, ores and anything else a pickaxe is meant for.
item.forgeweave.rapier.description: A quick, light blade. Every hit also tears out a fraction of the target's remaining health, straight through armour.
item.forgeweave.scimitar.description: A light curved blade. Its cuts keep bleeding after the swing, and fresh cuts stack on top of the ones already open.
item.forgeweave.scimitar.property.1: Cuts keep bleeding after the swing
item.forgeweave.scimitar.property.2: Fresh cuts stack up to three deep
item.forgeweave.scythe.description: Reaps a 3x3x3 of crops and replants them, and cuts everything around what it strikes.
item.forgeweave.shortbow.description: The Shortbow is a quick and nimble weapon. It allows for fast movements while shooting arrows at a rapid rate. Uses material and vanilla arrows.
item.forgeweave.shortbow.property.1: Can be used with vanilla arrows
item.forgeweave.shovel.description: Moves dirt, sand and gravel faster than your hands ever will.
item.forgeweave.shovel.property.1: Effective on dirt, sand and gravel
item.forgeweave.shuriken.description: The Shuriken is a fast, short ranged throwing weapon. It has high quantities but low damage. Can be thrown from the off-hand.
item.forgeweave.vein_hammer.description: Follows an ore vein through the stone, and shrugs armor aside.
item.forgeweave.vein_hammer.property.2: Mines a whole connected vein at once
item.forgeweave.warmace.description: A heavy flanged mace, forged at the Tool Forge. Strike while falling and the blow lands harder the further you fell, shoves everything nearby away, and leaves you unhurt by the landing.
item.forgeweave.warmace.property.2: Falling strikes hit far harder and knock everything nearby away
item.forgeweave.warmace.property.3: A landed smash spares you the fall damage
